title: perf(core,metadata-protocol): an authenticated data request pays 6 warm serial rounds instead of 8, and 3 with the landed opt-ins
body:
Fixes #10757. This PR carries the card's engine legs (leg 4, leg 5, the cold double resolution and leg 6) under claim 6264940865; leg A is ruled out at 6265874149 (#24515 closed not_planned), so every item is landed or ruled out once this lands.

Clause-②: no (no accept set, served body or authz answer moves: fewer queries and rounds for the same answer; owes the seat's review of record before the queue, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by the seat's choice, since it changes when authz and localization caches are trusted)

## What changed

An authenticated `GET /api/v1/data/OBJECT?$top=1` on the stock showcase (local PostgreSQL 16) now pays fewer rounds:

- warm admin: **11 queries / 6 rounds**, was 12 / 8;
- warm member: **10 / 6**, was 11 / 7;
- with the landed opt-ins on (grants cache TTL above 0, `$count=false`): **3 / 3**, was 4 / 4.

The served bodies and the resolved authz envelopes are unchanged.

- **Leg 4, landed** (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`). The Default Organization read (`sys_organization` by slug) and the activation-ledger read (`sys_metadata_activation`) are now one wave. Before, they were awaited one after the other.
  - While the organization read is open, the ledger is asked about every permission-set name that may apply.
  - One recorded widening: an organization-owned `admin_full_access` grant that turns out not to anchor platform standing adds `admin_full_access` to the ledger's `name IN` list. Nobody reads that verdict, and the envelope does not move.
  - ⛔ No predicate is edited. The organization read is still `{ slug: 'default' }` with limit 1. `grantAppliesInTenant` and `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` (the NULL-organization readings that the C8 lane holds, 6264887348) are called as before and not edited. A pin asserts the organization read byte-for-byte.
- **Leg 4, the duplicate `sys_user` read: ruled out here.** The two reads are better-auth's session-to-user read (plugin-auth's adapter) and `getUserRow` inside the `customSession` callback's `resolveUserAuthzGrants` call. `getUserRow` is already memoized within one resolution.
  - The callback's caller is in `plugin-auth`. better-auth's user deliberately does not carry `ai_access` (`auth-manager.ts`, the `user:` config note). So one read can serve both consumers only through a `plugin-auth` change (`domain:services`); no card carries it now (carrier: none), since #24515 closed `not_planned`.
  - Adding a core seed option that nothing passes would be a speculative surface, so none is added. See the report's `open_questions`.
- **Leg 5, landed** (the same file, `localizationCache`). A success entry is now retired only by:
  - a write that can change its answer: a write to `sys_setting` or `sys_platform_setting`, the two tables `SettingsService.getMany` and the direct fallback read, observed after it settles by an unkeyed engine middleware;
  - a non-`write` epoch reason (`remote`, `metadata`, `manual`);
  - the `localization` settings change seam;
  - the TTL.

  Before, any write to any object retired it. On an idle boot, the outbox pollers' claim updates were such writes.
  - The failure entry (#10221 / #11877) keeps its TTL-only rule. A pin proves that a watched write and a `remote` bump do not retire it.
  - A success is cached only on an engine with both the write epoch and `registerMiddleware`. With TTL `0` nothing is registered on the engine.
- **Cold, ruled out with its reading** (`request-grants-memo.ts`, the `attachedHere` guard in `commit`). The guard is load-bearing:
  - A one-shot reading (scratch test, not committed) on the memo suite's own doubles: a revocation that started before the observer existed and landed between the first request's two resolutions. With the guard, the request is authorised without the revoked `auditor` position. With the guard removed, it is served `auditor`.
  - A dist-only experiment with the guard removed measured the first request at 16 / 8 instead of 23 / 10, so the guard is the whole cause of the double resolution.
  - The only change that keeps the memo's argument whole is to register the observer before the first request: a boot-time seam, outside this card's file fence. It would save 7 queries and 2 rounds once per process. It is not built here (four-axis reasoning in the report).
- **Leg 6, landed in `packages/metadata-protocol` (this lane).** Nothing changes in `@objectstack/rest`, so nothing is declared to `domain:cli`.
  - `getMetaItem`, the served face that `enforceApiAccess` reads on every `/data` request, now reads the item's active `sys_metadata` rows through #11967's overlay cache, under a key naming the item. The protocol's own authoring reads still read the store (the private body, e.g. the destructive-change check before an object save).
  - The overlay cache, for the list read and the by-name read alike, is now retired by a `sys_metadata` write observed after it settles, by every non-`write` epoch reason (the metadata bridge's `remote` bump included), and by the TTL. #11633 §4's leg-D design names this trigger: "any engine-seam write to `sys_metadata`". Before, any write to any object retired it, so the outbox pollers and every user's data write made the next `/data` request read `sys_metadata` again.
- **Docs:** the `OS_LOCALIZATION_CACHE_TTL_MS` and `OS_METADATA_OVERLAY_CACHE_TTL_MS` rows (`content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`) and the overlay-cache note (`content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`) now state the new retirement rules.

## Reading: local PostgreSQL 16.15, method of 6255731843

- **Setup:** the stock showcase, `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p PORT --database postgres://…`, a fresh database per boot. Each request is `GET /api/v1/data/OBJECT?$top=1` with `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json`, 2.5 s apart. Per persona (admin, and `auditor.demo@example.com`), three objects (`sys_user_preference`, `showcase_task`, `sys_api_key`), four requests each.
- **Instrument:** a temporary per-query log in `SqlDriver.installQueryTiming`, applied to the source, built into `dist/` and then reverted. The source is blob-equal to `HEAD` and the dists were rebuilt clean afterwards. The admin's logged count equals `Server-Timing`'s `N queries` on every request.
- **Rounds:** a query that starts before the latest end of the current round joins it; otherwise it opens a new round.
- **Background write:** before each object's third request, one untimed `PATCH` of a `showcase_task` row. That object is unrelated to localization and to `sys_metadata`.
- **Runs:** `L` = behind a +20 ms RTT proxy (switched on after boot), `R` = direct.
- **Trees:** `main` = `913fd6df8a`. After = this branch merged with `origin/main` `f4755a68a`, head `4746b38c1`.

| case | `main` L1 / R1 | after L1 / R1 |
|:--|--:|--:|
| warm admin | 12 / 8 · 12 / 8 | **11 / 6** · **11 / 6** |
| warm member | 11 / 7 · 11 / 7 | **10 / 6** · **10 / 6** |
| first request after boot (admin) | 23 / 12 · 23 / 12 | 23 / 10 · 23 / 10 |
| warm, after a write to an unrelated object | 14 / 9 (admin), 13 / 8 (member): 6 of 6 retired localization | 11 / 6 and 10 / 6: 0 of 6 retired anything |
| opt-ins on (grants TTL 10000, `$count=false`), warm (L2c / R2c) | 4 / 4 · n/a | **3 / 3** · **3 / 3** |

The warm admin request after, per query (final-L1, `sys_user_preference` #2):

| # | round | query |
|--:|--:|:--|
| 1 | 1 | `sys_session` by token (better-auth) |
| 2 | 2 | `sys_user` by id (better-auth's fallback join, leg A) |
| 3–7 | 3 | wave 1: `sys_user`, `sys_member` ×2, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_user_position` |
| 8–9 | 4 | `sys_organization` by slug **and** `sys_metadata_activation` (was rounds 4 and 5) |
| 10 | 5 | the data SELECT |
| 11 | 6 | the COUNT |

- **Gone from the warm request:** `sys_metadata` by name (was round 6). The localization pair is gone too, except at its 30 s TTL (the two remaining misses in each run land 30.4 s and 30.1 s after the key's first read).
- **The member's request:** the same, without `sys_organization`.
- **Opt-ins on:** `sys_session`, `sys_user`, the SELECT.
- **Wall time, illustrative only:** a synthetic RTT, not deployment evidence, and ⛔ no claim about cloud#1521's gate or cloud#1518's placement. With the proxy, the warm admin DB span is 207 ms on `main` and 169 ms after. With the opt-ins on it is 111 ms and 79 ms.

**Controls (byte identity, normalized for per-boot random ids and timestamps):**
- The resolved authz envelope (positions, permissions, `org_user_ids`, `accessible_org_ids`, posture, tab permissions) is one distinct value per persona, and it is identical on `main` and after, in every pair compared (main-R1 against final-R1 and final-L1; main-L2c against final-L2c and final-R2c).
- Served bodies: 24 / 24 identical for main-R1 against final-R1, and against the intermediate leg run.
- Across other boot pairs, `showcase_task` picks a different seeded row under `order by id asc limit 1`, because seeded ids are random per boot. The titles differ; the keys and totals do not. `sys_user_preference` and `sys_api_key` are identical in every pair.

## Pins and ablations

Each ablation mutates only this package's source, and the subject is imported by a relative specifier, so no rebuild leg applies. Each restore was checked blob-equal to `HEAD`.

- **Leg 4:** `resolve-authz-context.request-rounds.test.ts` (new, 5 cases). The envelope written out, the reads issued, and 2 legs.
  - Ablation: the base resolver restored. 4 of 5 red. Three of them red on the leg count alone (`expected 3 to be 2`), with the envelope and reads asserted green before it. The fourth is the recorded widening, red on the ledger read.
- **Leg 5:** `resolve-localization-cache.test.ts`. Its doubles now carry the engine's middleware seam. New pins:
  - writes to `sys_http_delivery`, `sys_notification_delivery`, `showcase_task` and `sys_session` do not retire the entry, with zero reads;
  - a `sys_platform_setting` write retires it;
  - the retirement lands after the write settles;
  - `metadata` and `remote` bumps retire it;
  - no middleware seam means no cache;
  - TTL `0` registers nothing;
  - the failure memo survives a watched write.

  Ablation: the leg-4 version of the file restored. 9 red, the in-flight case among them.
- **Leg 6:** `protocol.item-read-overlay-cache.test.ts` (new, 7 cases) and a new `meta-overlay-cache.test.ts` §10.
  - Ablation 1: `servedRead` set to `false`. 4 red; the authoring-read, no-seam and TTL-0 controls stay green.
  - Ablation 2: the epoch-keyed `meta-overlay-cache.ts` and `protocol.ts` restored. 10 red.
  - The prolongation suite's double gained the middleware seam so that its arms still run against a live cache. Ablation: `applyRemoteMetadataMutation`'s `bumpWriteEpoch` removed. 3 red.
- **Pin sweep:** `request-grants-memo*` does not move. The `resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence` goldens do not move (no fixture holds an organization-owned `admin_full_access`). `rest-data-read-one-overlay-read.test.ts` does not move: its engine has no write-epoch seam, so the cache declines there, as before. The rest/hono localization pins pass unchanged.
  - Moved: the doubles in `resolve-localization-cache.test.ts`, `meta-overlay-cache.test.ts` and `protocol.datasource-delete-prolongation.test.ts`, each to carry the seam a real engine has.
  - `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` learned the new suite's `findOne` double (`--write`).

## Verification (head `4746b38c1`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0. `--listFiles` counts the new and edited test files in both programs.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test`: exit 0, 106 files / 2580 tests. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test:repo`: exit 0, 6 / 82.
- `metadata-protocol` vitest: exit 0, 248 files passed and 3 skipped, 20723 tests.
- The rest one-overlay-read and business-timezone pins: 46 / 46. The plugin-hono-server localization pin: 13 / 13.
- `turbo run build` (all 76 packages) after merging `origin/main`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths) derived 109 families. Every one was run with its exit code captured before any pipe, and all exited 0 (`check:engine-double-contract` after the ledger write). `--ran`: "109 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 109 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)".
- **Fix round 1 (head `084e79e16`), for `Test Core (5/6)`:** `environment-overlay-five-types.test.ts` stored its overlay row with `driver.create` after a control read that now fills the by-name overlay cache, so no engine middleware saw the write. The row now goes through `engine.insert` under a system context, as every production writer does. No cache was disabled, no TTL changed and no assertion was weakened. Before: exit 1, 10 failed. After: 26 / 26. A sweep of the tests that write `sys_metadata`, `sys_setting` or `sys_platform_setting` straight into a driver found no other one that reads before it writes. Full suites at `084e79e16`, each exit 0: objectql 446 / 8392, runtime 422 files, rest 300 files, plugin-security 188 files, service-settings 51 / 881, plugin-hono-server 34 / 422, mcp 40 / 479. objectql and rest typecheck exit 0. `--ran` over both rounds: "111 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 111 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)".

## Acceptance notes

- **Still paid, for the card's remaining lane:** leg A's second round, ruled out under the current engine contract (6265874149); the duplicate `sys_user` read (needs a `plugin-auth` seed; carrier: none); the cold double resolution (a boot-time observer registration); and the COUNT unless `$count=false`.
- **Grants cache default unchanged:** with its default of `0` (#11633 Fork 4, the maintainer's), leg B still costs 2 rounds per warm request. This PR does not move it.
- **What the after-reading shows:** with the landed opt-ins on, the warm request is already at 3 rounds before leg A lands. With leg A it would be 2.
- **The ⚠️ pre-registration write:** the localization and overlay observers register on the first read that names an engine. A write that started before that registration never passes them. The epoch reading they replace was blind to it as well, and the TTL bounds it. Stated in both docblocks.
- **The transaction window:** the localization and overlay caches are retired when a watched write's statement completes. Inside an engine transaction that comes before the commit, so a read landing between the two can keep the pre-commit rows until the next watched write or the TTL. The epoch reading this replaced had the same window. Stated in `metadata-lifecycle.mdx` and `environment-variables.mdx`.
